Its name is Creative Commons Attribution Non Commercial Share Alike 3.0 Unported. Its licenseText heading uses Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported. GitHub's SPDX license-list-data tag object 76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b names v3.29.0 and directly targets commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48, the revision in the detail URL. The API reports an unsigned tag. Repository provenance supports the documented target.

As context, the complete CC capture at the cited URL has digest e047257153dc2257462417add4db78c5f584c10630919288e95af7cf2ed1a474 and the claimed inline title. The linked deed, plain text and RDF are separate representations. SPDX supplies the list membership.

challenge.method: Tested whether the US example in SPDX §4(b) identified a jurisdiction port, and whether the two ShareAlike records could be exchanged. Compared §3 and §4(b) in the generated text and the publisher capture.
challenge.results: SPDX §4(b) gives a 3.0 US example where CC gives a 3.0 Unported example. The closing paragraph of §3 points to §4(e) in SPDX and §4(d) in CC. These are concrete wording differences. The SPDX identifier, text heading and cited URL still select the unported by-nc-sa reference. Substituting by-sa loses the NC element and changes the URL.

limitations: The finding covers this generated record at the tagged commit. Its deprecation field concerns the SPDX identifier. Index maintenance, publisher currency, legal effect and release authorization have separate evidence.

The CC digest measures the acquired /legalcode response. Its canonical /legalcode.en declaration does not establish byte equality. The crosswalk establishes neither semantic equivalence nor rights concerning translations, adaptations, redistribution or downstream project files.
